name: A3, Association for Advancing Automation: the association's own landing page
title: A3, Association for Advancing Automation: the association's own landing page
answer: This is the home page of the Association for Advancing Automation, known as A3. It is a landing page rather than a report, and it carries no order statistics, dates or figures. Its most useful content is a statement of scope: the association says it combines robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and AI, and that it connects innovators, businesses and technologies across robotics, vision, motion control and industrial AI to accelerate progress in automation.

sections.body: The source is the home page of the Association for Advancing Automation, published by the association itself on its own site at automate.org. It is a landing page, not a report, dataset, press release or standards document. Its scope, as the page describes it, is the association's own remit across robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and AI. The page states no publication date and no author. The copy used here was harvested on 29 September 2026, which is when the page was captured rather than a date the page itself gives.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page consists of two short pieces of text. The first describes A3 as combining robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and AI into what it calls a comprehensive hub for information on the latest technologies. That sentence appears twice in the harvested copy, once as the page description and once as visible text. The second piece says the association connects innovators, businesses and technologies across key technology sectors, naming robotics, vision, motion control and industrial AI, in order to accelerate progress in automation. Nothing else is present. There is no list of member companies, no explanation of how the association is organised, no description of its events, standards work or publications, and no data of any kind. The page does not mention manufacturing directly, nor does it mention order statistics, machine vision integration or sensor density. A reader looking for the quarterly figures the industry page refers to will not find them here. What the page does establish is the association's own account of its remit, which spans robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and industrial AI.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, no dates and no definitions of metrics. Its only claims are about scope: that A3 combines robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and AI, and that it connects innovators, businesses and technologies across robotics, vision, motion control and industrial AI to accelerate progress in automation.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in manufacturing would use this page only to identify what A3 says it covers, which is robotics, vision, imaging, motion control, motors and industrial AI, and to confirm that the association positions itself as a hub connecting businesses and technologies in those areas. It is a starting point for finding the association's other material, not a source of evidence. The claim on the industry page about quarterly order statistics, machine vision integration and sensor density is not supported by anything on this page, so anyone citing A3 for those figures needs to go to a different document on the same site.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Manufacturing

sections.body: This is a promotional landing page written by the organisation it describes, so it is self-interested and carries no independent verification. It contains no data, no dates, no methodology and no manufacturing-specific content. It does not cover robotics deployment, machine vision integration, sensor density or order statistics, which are the things the industry page cites A3 for. It is partial in the plain sense that it is a fragment of a larger site, and it is undated, so a reader cannot tell how current its description of the association is.
